note: Official certification objectives, recorded so every lesson can be traced to a real exam objective. Dates are the day each was checked against the publisher's own material. Anything not confirmed against a primary source is marked verified:false and must not be quoted as an exam fact.

exams.title: Cisco CCNA 200-301
exams.sourceNote: Official Cisco exam topics PDF, published 2026-05-14. Cisco's marketing pages still say v1.1; the PDF is the authority.

domains.name: AI, and Network Operations and Management

subtopics.text: Interpret a routing table to identify the next hop (prefix/mask, administrative distance, metric, default route)
Troubleshoot IPv4 and IPv6 static routing: default, network, host, floating static
Configure single-area OSPFv2 for IPv4 and OSPFv3 for IPv6
Interpret the operational status of FHRP (HSRP and VRRP)
Configure and verify VLANs
Configure and verify trunking on a switched network
Configure and verify STP
Describe the purpose and operation of switch port security, DHCP snooping and DAI
Manage device configuration and software files using secure file transfer (SFTP/SCP)
Configure NAT/PAT on IOS XE routers
Diagnose issues with DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR)
Configure IPv4 ACLs (standard, extended, numbered, named)
Configure Layer 2 security features: DHCP snooping, DAI, storm control, RA guard, port security
Describe the interaction of common application layer protocols
Describe modern network infrastructure and architecture
Describe network management approaches (device-based, cloud, controller, automation, IaC)

exams.title: CompTIA A+
exams.sourceNote: Current exam codes are 220-1201 / 220-1202, live since March 2025 and retiring 2027-2028. Domain weights below are from the published objectives. The 220-1101/220-1102 generation is retired.

subtopics.text: Troubleshoot motherboard, RAM, CPU and power issues
Storage: HDD, SSD, NVMe, RAID, M.2, and drive partitioning
Apply the troubleshooting process: identify the problem, establish theory, test, plan, verify
TCP and UDP ports and protocols; IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnet mask, gateway
Virtualization concepts, hypervisors, virtual machine requirements
Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows: recovery, safe mode, startup repair, bootrec, bcdedit, BSOD
Windows settings, features and editions; common operating systems
Security fundamentals: physical security, passwords, MFA, encryption, secure connections

exams.title: MikroTik Certified Network Associate
exams.code: MTCNA training outline (last edited January 2016; syllabus still published)
exams.sourceNote: MikroTik's own published training outline. Note it predates RouterOS 7 — the syllabus is still the published one, but every command must be checked against current RouterOS documentation.

domains.name: Module 1 — Introduction: RouterOS, RouterBOARD, CLI, backups vs export
Module 2 — DHCP: server, client, leases, network config, ARP
Module 5 — Wireless (basic): connect list, WPA-PSK/WPA2-PSK, monitoring
Module 6 — Firewall: principles, connection tracking, chains, filter, address list, src NAT, masquerade, dst NAT, redirect, FastTrack
Module 7 — QoS: simple queues, targets, PCQ
Module 8 — Tunnels: PPP, PPPoE, pools, secure local networking
Module 9 — Misc: support output, logs, backups, network diagrams

subtopics.text: DHCP server network configuration and lease management
ARP modes and the RouterOS ARP table
Bridge concepts; adding and managing bridge ports; restoring configuration from backup
Static routing, default routes, route distance and gateway reachability
Firewall filter: structure, chains and actions
Protecting the router (input chain)
Protecting customers (forward chain)
Source NAT: masquerade and src-nat actions
Destination NAT: dst-nat and redirect actions
Managing configuration backups; difference between backup (.backup) and export (.rsc)
RouterOS CLI principles and menu navigation

exams.title: MikroTik Certified Routing Engineer
exams.sourceNote: Prerequisite: MTCNA. Covers static routing in depth, OSPFv2, VPN and VLAN.

domains.name: Module 1 — Static Routing: more specific routes, ECMP, route distance, recursive next-hop
Module 3 — VPN: IPIP, EoIP, PPTP, SSTP, L2TP, PPPoE, VLAN, QinQ
Module 4 — OSPF: areas, router types, DR/BDR election, LSA types, cost, SPT, stub, NSSA, virtual links

subtopics.text: More specific routes and ECMP (equal-cost multi-path)
Gateway reachability check and route distance
OSPF neighbours and neighbour states, DR and BDR election
VLAN and its usage; VLAN on managed switches

Configure networking: NetworkManager, nmcli, name resolution
Boot and shutdown; select a boot target; use systemd and journald

exams.title: Windows Server / Microsoft platform role-based certifications
exams.code: Role-based (for example AZ-800 Windows Server Hybrid; role assessments)
exams.verifyNote: NOT verified. Microsoft has retired most of the old MCSA/MCSE Windows Server certifications and moved to role-based credentials, so there is no single 'Windows Server exam' to map against. The task areas below are the standard operational responsibilities an administrator is expected to cover, NOT an extracted official objective list. Treat as a coverage checklist, not as an exam blueprint.
exams.checked: 2026-10-10 (general knowledge; not extracted from an official objectives document)

domains.name: Active Directory Domain Services — forests, domains, OUs, Group Policy, DNS integration
Networking services — DHCP, DNS, IP configuration
File and print services, NTFS and share permissions
Remote administration, PowerShell, Windows Admin Center
Security hardening, BitLocker, auditing, least privilege
Backup, recovery, Windows Backup and Veeam Agent

subtopics.text: Deploy and manage Active Directory Domain Services; forests, domains, trusts
Administer users, groups, computers and OUs with PowerShell (AD cmdlets)
Deploy and troubleshoot Group Policy; security filtering
Deploy and manage DHCP; scopes, options, reservations, failover
Deploy and manage DNS; zones, records, delegation, AD-integrated zones
Deploy and manage file services; NTFS permissions vs share permissions
